chunks: I transported Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) for the second time to al-Kufa, while Abu Ja'far al-Mansur was stationed there. When he drew near to al-Hashimiyya — the city of Abu Ja'far — he withdrew his foot from the stirrup, dismounted, called for a grey mule, and dressed in white garments and a white skullcap.

When he entered upon him, Abu Ja'far said to him: 'You have likened yourself to the Prophets.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) replied: 'And how can you distance me from the descendants of the Prophets?' He then said: 'I had resolved to send to Medina someone who would uproot its palm trees and take its offspring captive.' He (the Imam) said: 'And why is that, O Commander of the Faithful?'

He replied: 'It has been reported to me that your servant al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays is calling people to you and gathering wealth for you.' He (the Imam) said: 'By God, that is not the case.' He said: 'I will not be satisfied with you unless you swear by divorce, emancipation, sacrifice, and pilgrimage on foot.' He (the Imam) said: 'Are you commanding me to swear by rivals besides God? Truly, the one who is not satisfied with God has no part with God in anything.'

He said: 'Are you teaching me jurisprudence?' He (the Imam) replied: 'And how can you distance me from jurisprudence, when I am the son of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace be upon him and his family)?' He said: 'Then I shall bring you face to face with the one who informed against you.' He (the Imam) said: 'Do so.' The man who had informed against him came forward. Abu Abdillah said to him: 'O you!' He said: 'Yes, by God — Who, there is no god but He, the Knower of the unseen and the seen, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful — I indeed did it.'

So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Woe to you! You are glorifying God so that He would be too ashamed to punish you. But say: I disavow the might and power of God, and I rely upon my own might and power.' The man swore by that, and before he could finish the oath, he fell down dead. Abu Ja'far said to him (the Imam): 'I will never give credence to anyone against you henceforth.' And he treated him generously and sent him on his way.

key_terms.الطَّلَاق وَالْعَتَاق وَالْهَدْي وَالْمَ: Divorce, emancipation, sacrifice, and pilgrimage on foot: four types of oaths used in common practice but not sanctioned as legally binding in Shia jurisprudence
key_terms.الْأَنْدَاد: Rivals/equals: those set as partners besides God, used here for forms of oath that invoke other than God
key_terms.الْمُعَلَّى بْنَ خُنَيْسٍ: Al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays: a close companion and agent of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), martyred by the Abbasids
key_terms.الْهَاشِمِيَّة: Al-Hashimiyya: the new Abbasid capital city built by al-Mansour near Kufa before the construction of Baghdad
key_terms.حَوْل اللَّه وَقُوَّته: The might and power of God: a Quranic/liturgical phrase (حَوْلَ اللَّهِ وَقُوَّتِهِ), disavowal of which is tantamount to apostasy

ai.seo_question: What happened when Imam al-Sadiq was brought before the Abbasid Caliph al-Mansour?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a confrontation between Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) and the Abbasid Caliph al-Mansour (r. 136–158 AH/754–775 CE) at al-Hashimiyya, the caliph's new capital near Kufa. The Imam had been summoned under suspicion that his associate al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays was raising funds for a rebellion. When al-Mansour demanded oaths by divorce, emancipation, sacrifice, and pilgrimage — forms with no basis in Quranic oath-law — the Imam refused on theological grounds, asserting that God alone is the proper object of oaths. The dramatic climax shows the Imam instructing the false informant to repudiate God's power, upon which the man swore and immediately died, vindicating the Imam completely. This incident took place shortly before the execution of al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays in 148 AH.
word_analysis: so that He would be ashamed

When we arrived at Al-Hashimiyya, a city of Abu Ja’far, he<sup>asws</sup> extracted his<sup>asws</sup> leg from the stirrups, then descended and called for a young mule, and wore white clothes and a white headgear.

So when he<sup>asws</sup> went over to him, Abu Ja’far said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘You<sup>asws</sup> have resembled yourself<sup>asws</sup> with the Prophets<sup>as</sup>’. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And it means you are distancing me<sup>asws</sup> from the sons<sup>asws</sup> of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>’.

So he said, ‘It has been raised to me that your<sup>asws</sup> slave Al-Moala Bin Khunays is calling (people) to you<sup>asws</sup> and is gathering the wealth for you<sup>asws</sup>’. en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from certain persons of his people from Safwan al-Jammal who has said the following: “I provided abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, transportation to al-Kufah for the second time and abu Ja‘far al-Mansur was in it. When he (the Imam) arrived in al-Hashimiyah, the city of abu Ja‘far, al- Mansur, he (the Imam) pulled out his feet from the saddle’s stirrups and dismounted. He asked for al- Shahba ’ mule and dressed in white, with a white hat.

When he (the Imam) entered the place of abu Ja‘far al-Mansur he said, ‘You have dressed like the Prophets.’ Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘Why do you want to distance me from the children of the Prophets?’ Abu Ja‘far al-Mansur said, ‘I was planning to send to al-Madinah an army to uproot all its palm trees, take all of its inhabitants as captives.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘Why did you want to do so, O ’Amir al-Mu’minin?’

abu Ja‘far al- Mansur said, ‘Because I am informed that your slave Mu‘alla’ ibn Khunayth calls people to you and collects funds for you.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘By Allah it is not true.’ Abu Ja‘far al-Mansur said, ‘I cannot agree with you unless it is swearing to divorce, setting free of slaves, sacrificial offering and walking (Sa‘y).’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Are you commanding me to swear by things as partners of Allah? One who is not happy with Allah has no case with Allah.’

Abu Ja‘far al-Mansur said, ‘Are you showing me how great your knowledge of the law is?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Why do you distance me from understanding and law when I am a child of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause?’ Abu Ja‘far al- Mansur said, ‘I will bring the informer face to face with you.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘You can definitely do so.’ The informer came and abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, asked him, ‘O so and so.’ He replied, ‘Yes, by Allah, besides whom no one deserves to be worshipped, who knows the unseen and seen, the Beneficent, the Merciful that you have done so (called people to yourself . . .).’

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said to him, ‘Woe is on you! Are you glorifying Allah so that He may feel embarrassed to punish you?’ You must say, ‘I denounce the means and power of Allah and I resort to my own means and power.’ The man then took the oath the way he was told but before completing he dropped dead.’ Abu Ja‘far al-Mansur then said, ‘I will not believe anyone thereafter against you.’ He gave him (the Imam) good rewards and allowed him to go back.’”
